memory_update.text: LOPE should remain a reference anchor for hybrid ABSN/OTA capacity because its disclosures explicitly mention hybrid pillar growth, ABSN/OTA graduates, simulation technology, VR, prerequisite strategies, and employer relationships.

ATGE is a direct healthcare education capacity benchmark through Chamberlain, Walden, and medical/veterinary schools; key watch items are clinical-site capacity, program accreditation, and student-financing rules.

HSTM is an underfollowed picks-and-shovels candidate for healthcare education capacity because its clinical learning, credentialing, scheduling, and rotation-compliance products may support the bottleneck without being labeled as education exposure.
UTI is an underfollowed healthcare education capacity candidate via Concorde Career Colleges; the healthcare exposure may be obscured by the company's transportation and skilled-trades branding.

For this node, the bottleneck is not generic online learning; it is licensure-linked hybrid capacity requiring physical campuses, simulation labs, clinical placements, instructors, employer/hospital partnerships, accreditation, and state approvals.

Need a separate supplier pass for private or non-US-listed simulation and clinical-placement vendors such as healthcare simulation equipment, VR training, licensure-prep, and clinical-placement workflow software; many pure-play chokepoints may not be public.

node: Hybrid healthcare education capacity: ABSN, OTA, nursing, counseling, social work, simulation, and clinical infrastructure
summary: Expanded the universe around the hybrid healthcare-training capacity node with a two-lane funnel. Reference anchors are Grand Canyon Education and Adtalem because they directly operate or enable licensure-linked healthcare programs at scale. The more underfollowed discovery lane includes HealthStream as a software/workforce-infrastructure supplier tied to clinical learning, credentialing, scheduling, and rotations, and Universal Technical Institute via Concorde Career Colleges as a less obvious healthcare-training campus operator hidden under a transportation/skilled-trades label. Key chokepoint variables to verify next are clinical placement capacity, simulation-lab utilization, employer/hospital partnerships, regulatory approvals, campus openings, Title IV exposure, and program-level enrollment growth.
